name: Wolfsklamm
kurzbeschreibung: The wildly romantic Wolfsklamm gorge near Stans thrills hikers with 354 wooden stairs, thundering waterfalls, and the pilgrimage trail to St. Georgenberg.
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular Wolfsklamm gorge near Stans in the lower Tyrolean Inn Valley counts among the most sublime, oldest, and most storied natural canyons in the Eastern Alps. First opened to intrepid hikers back in 1901, this awe-inspiring limestone chasm on the sunny southern flanks of the Karwendel Nature Park has magnetically drawn mountain enthusiasts ever since. Over countless millennia, the fierce Stallenbach mountain stream carved deeply into the hard limestone bedrock, creating an astonishing natural wonderland: surging emerald-green mountain waters plummet over countless cascades, while vertical rock walls close in to within just a few meters of one another.

Route & Requirements

An adventurous, masterfully constructed trail leads safely through the roaring labyrinth over a total of 354 wooden stair steps, suspended galleries, and pathways carved directly into the bare stone cliffs. Hikers experience the raw primal power of alpine white water up close, enjoying cooling mineral mist on warm summer days. At the canyon's upper threshold, the gorge widens into a serene alpine riverbank with gravel flats ideal for resting. From here, a signposted forest path crosses the daring, heritage-protected Hohe Brücke stone-and-timber bridge up to the rock monastery of St. Georgenberg, Tyrol's oldest pilgrimage sanctuary perched eagle-like on a sheer rock monolith. Surefootedness and sturdy hiking footwear are essential.

Visit & Arrival

The Wolfsklamm gorge is open daily from early May to early November between 09:00 and 16:30 (closed in winter due to ice and rockfall hazard). The uphill ascent through the gorge takes approximately one hour of pure walking time. Admission fees: adults approx. €7.00, children €3.00. Arrival by car: via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Schwaz) to Stans, where paid parking is located right at the gorge entrance. By train: ÖBB regional trains stop at Stans bei Schwaz station, from which an easy, signposted fifteen-minute walk through the village reaches the ticket booth.

Tips

Sturdy hiking boots with non-slip tread and good balance are indispensable for the climb; the narrow wooden stairways are unsuitable for strollers or wheelchairs. Following the ascent, the traditional pilgrimage inn at St. Georgenberg offers hearty refreshments with sweeping mountain views of the Karwendel range. For the return leg, take the gentler circular trail via Maria Tax and the Way of the Cross back down to Stans, absorbing fresh impressions of Tyrol's alpine landscapes.
preis: Adults approx. €7.00, children (6–14 years) €3.00, under 6 free
oeffnungszeiten: Open daily from May to early November 09:00–16:30 (closed in winter)
